newsitem.title: HONG KONG: HK stocks end with strong gains, led by property.
newsitem.headline: HK stocks end with strong gains, led by property.

text.p: Property counters were back in the limelight on Monday after their recent dull performance, leading Hong Kong stocks to a strong close as investors anticipated a strong response to upcoming property sales.
The Hang Seng Index closed on a gain of 108.56 points, or 0.81 percent, at 13,507.28. Turnover was HK$9.91 billion compared with HK$11.64 billion on Friday.
The Hang Seng properties sub-index surged 490.53 points, or 1.96 percent, to 25,506.54.
"They have been slow for almost two months," said Antony Mak, sales director at Vickers Ballas.
"They beginning to come back. It's rotational buying," said Mak.

Cheung Kong (Holdings) Ltd led the sector as investors anticipated strong demand for flats at its Laguna Verde development in Hunghom, Kowloon. Brokers said flats were expected to be offered at about HK$8,000 per square foot.
Cheung Kong shares rose HK$2.75 to HK$76.75.
Also in the property sector, Sun Hung Kai Properties Ltd gained HK$1.25 to HK$90.75 and Henderson Land Development Co Ltd rose HK$1.75 to HK$71.00.

HSBC Holdings Plc ended flat at HK$189.00 ahead of its results. After the close, HSBC announced a 23 percent rise in 1996 pretax profit to 4.52 billion sterling. "It is pretty much on the dot. However we are still going to see a bit of pressure on this," said Kent Rossiter, institutional sales manager at Nikko Securities.
"In line with expectations is not good enough to support the share price. I would not expect much in the short term," he said, adding however that the stock was still a buy.
Hang Seng Bank Ltd posted a 6.3 percent rise in 1996 net profit to HK$8.49 billion after the close.
The stock closed at HK$89.00, down HK$0.50.

Corporate results are expected to dictate the market's direction over the coming weeks, although investors will also be watching U.S. economic data closely following U.S. Federal Reserve chairman Alan Greenspan's warning last week that interest rates could rise.
"We will still be locked in a range over the next few weeks. We will be results driven," said Mak.
Shares in Great Eagle Holdings Ltd jumped HK$1.85 to HK$30.90 after the company shelved plans to spin off its Tai Shan Properties Ltd arm.
